verdict.reasoning: Patient states decreased hearing in the left ear: 'I just feel like I can't really hear as well as I used to' and confirms it's the left ear only and duration 'For about six weeks.' and 'Just the left ear, yeah.'

Transcript notes decreased hearing in the left ear but does not describe it as 'muffled' or specify that the hearing loss is intermittent: 'I just feel like I can't really hear as well as I used to.' The doctor later mentions muffled hearing as a possible result of wax as an explanation, not as a reported symptom.

Patient reports triggers for the ringing: 'It's kind of on and off. Like some things trigger it as well. So, for example, if I'm watching TV or listening to music or something. Something that will set off the ringing in the ear.' and earlier specifies it is the left ear: 'ringing in my left ear just on the one side.'

Patient describes mild dizziness and imbalance: 'there's actually been a few times when I felt kind of a bit sick or a bit dizzy as well' and later clarifies 'Nothing major... not proper room spinning or anything like that, but just a little bit kind of off balance.'

Patient mentions mild nausea-like feeling: 'there's actually been a few times when I felt kind of a bit sick' and distinguishes it from severe nausea: 'It's not that kind of dizziness you get with nausea, like not proper room spinning...' This supports mild nausea/feeling sick.

Patient reports a prior similar short episode: 'I had something maybe about a year ago, but it only lasted a couple of days. It wasn't anything as long as this.' This matches a similar episode one year ago lasting a few days.

Doctor asks about these symptoms and patient’s responses imply denial: ear pain (doctor: 'And have you had any pain from the ear at all?' no verbal answer but moves on, implying no), discharge ('Any discharge coming out of the ear?' similarly skipped to next), fever ('Have you been experiencing any fever?' patient: 'Not specifically, apart from the dizziness and sickness I mentioned before.'), itching ('has your ear been itchy at all?' patient: 'No.'), vertigo/room spinning ('not proper room spinning or anything like that'), chest pain ('Have you any chest pain with it?' patient: 'No.'), palpitations ('Any palpitations? Heartbeat and fast.' no affirmative answer, doctor moves on). Overall consistent with denials listed.
Doctor asks: 'Now, do you use cotton wool buds to try and clean out wax from your ears?' Patient replies: 'No. I don't know.' indicating he does not use cotton buds.
Consult is clearly remote: 'I'm Dr. Dean Mirza from Babylon... you can speak to her and we'll serve a video.' No vital signs or physical examination are described anywhere in the transcript.

Doctor discusses left-sided hearing loss with tinnitus and possible wax vs other causes: 'you've had ringing, difficulty hearing in your left ear' and 'Simple things might be wax... which can lead to muffled hearing... we need to exclude that first and then after that we can consider other potential possibilities.' and 'It might be that there's a problem inside the drum or the balance system...' This aligns with assessment of left hearing loss with tinnitus and differential of impacted cerumen versus other otologic pathology.

Dizziness is described as mild and likely ear-related: patient: 'Nothing major... just a little bit kind of off balance.' Doctor: 'It might be that there's a problem inside the drum or the balance system within the ear...' and he plans routine follow-up within 4–5 days, implying low acuity.

Doctor plans face-to-face GP clinic visit within 4–5 days for ear exam and possible wax: 'maybe if we book you in for a face to face appointment in one of our clinics... within the next four, five days or so' and 'one of the GP will just have a quick look down the ear, figure out whether there's a physical blockage...' and discusses impacted wax as the simple thing to exclude.

Doctor states admin will handle booking and patient should call: 'I'll send a message to our admin team, I'll ask them to slot you into one of our clinics in that time frame.' and 'I'll leave the number in the notes of this appointment, ring them, and then they'll stop you in.'

Doctor will provide tinnitus information via a link in the notes: 'I'm going to put paste the link for a leaflet about tinnitus in the notes for this appointment. I'd really appreciate it if you could start reading about it.'

'If there's any problem, any issues between now and when the clinic appointment is, just book another appointment and you can speak to her and we'll serve a video.' This advises patient to rebook sooner if symptoms change or problems arise.
